baselineDisplay.title: Marketing Across Cultures
baselineDisplay.text:
Almost all of us have heard about General Motors trying to sell their Nova model in Latin America and finding out that “no va” in Spanish literally means “it doesn’t go”. And of course, there was the famous first try of Coca Cola in China, when the translation of the soft drink’s name read “bite the wax tadpole”.
我们几乎都听说过这样一个销售案例:美国通用汽车公司试图在拉丁美洲销售他们的 Nova 车型，结果发现在西班牙语中，“no va” 的字面意思是“它走不了”。当然，同样有名的还有另外一个案例:可口可乐第一次登陆中国市场时，这种软饮料的名字被译成“蛾蚌啃蜡”。
But cultural awareness in marketing is a lot more than careful translation. There are subtleties and nuances to every culture, and there are just plain tablls. Although most people wouldn’t be able to list the rules of their own culture, they certainly know when those rules are violated. Our own culture tendd to be “invisible” to us, while differences we run into when abroad strike as strange, funny or extrotic. So how much more difficult it to discern the unwritten rules of another country?
但是市场营销中的文化意识却远远不只是小心谨慎的翻译而已。每一种文化都有它的微妙和特别之处，同时还有一些直白的忌讳。虽然大多数人都无法详尽地罗列出他们自己文化中的条条框框，但他们却肯定知道什么时候人们违背了他们的文化传统。对我们来说，自己所属的文化往往是看不见的，但是，当我们身处异地时，我们碰到的文化差异却令我们感到古怪、有趣或奇特。因此，要辨明另一国家不成文的规定到底有多么困难呢?
There is still no substitute for a visit to the target market. When in a foreign place, you’ll undoubtedly become aware of different aesthetica. What flavors, which colors, are used to attract buyers there? Foods you find unpalatable and decorations you find garish have completely different effects on the natives. Your hosts might ask seemingly rude questions such as “How old are you?” and “How much money do you make?” Meals, schedules, transportation, and personal conveniences can't be taken for granted. Prices for the simplest purchases are subject to negotiation. You haven't figured out all the small coins, and you don't understand anyone's name. And it just doesn't smell like home.
看来，去目标市场进行调查仍然是不二之选了。当你身处异国他乡时，你就肯定会留意到审美观的差异。在那里，到底哪些味道或颜色更容易吸引购买者?你觉得很难吃的东西或很艳俗的装饰品对当地人来说就完全是另一回事。主人可能会问客人一些看似不礼貌的间题，如“你多大啦?”或“你赚多少钱啊?”饮食、日程表、交通、个人便利等等都不能想当然。即便是购买最普通的物品，你也可以讨价还价。你没弄清楚所有的硬币，你也不懂任何人名字的含意。总之，一切都与在国内时不一样。
A visit is a golden opportunity to absorb the present-day culture. Every detail that differs from your usual pattern is a clue to the nationals. But also remember that learning the basics of comportment in another culture, though very important in your relationships with clients and contacts, isn't sufficient for planning a full marketing campaign. The simplest cultural differences can strand the grandest plans.
到目标市场走走也是吸收当今文化的黄金时机。任何与你平时生活模式有所不同的细节都能透露出当地居民的行为方式。但同样要记住的是，在培养和发展与客户或联系人的社会关系时，学会另一文化的规范行为举止虽然很重要，但这并不足以助你做一个全面的营销策划。最简单的文化差异也能搁浅最宏伟的计划。
In Japan, for example, a major household products company spent many millions of dollars on a marketing campaign in advance of introducing its laundry detergent. Nevertheless, when the detergent was made available, sales were miniscule. In fact, few shops stocked the soap. Non-tariff trade barriers? No, it was something much simpler. The typically US “large, economy-sized” boxes were far too big and bulky for the tiny Japanese retail establishments. And Japanese housewives don't usually have cars——they walk to the stores and carry their purchases home, to very small living spaces.
例如，在将其洗涤剂引入日本市场之前，一家大型的家用产品公司花了数百万美金进行了市场营销活动。尽管如此，当他们的洗涤剂在日本上市时，销量却客客无几。事实上，几乎没有商店储备这种肥皂。是非关税贸易壁垒的缘故吗?不是，真正的原因要简单得多。典型的美国式经济大包装对于空间狭小的日本零售店来说俨然是“庞然大物”。而且，日本的家庭主妇一般没有车，她们步行到商店，然后买了商品拎回家—个很小的处所。
Cultural factors influence consumer behavior. These factors include religion, superstation, family structure, cuisine, language and local history but estend to attitudes about such issues as government, work authority, age, environment, space and time, and male-female relationships. Finally, there is that difficult-to-define national sense of humor which often doesn't translate from one culture to another. Beyond concrete demographics, these attitudes are not as easy to circumscribe and pin down; besides, attitudes, even culturally ingrained ones, do change.
不同的文化因素—不仅包括宗教、迷信、家庭结构、饮食、语言和当地的历史，还延伸到对待事物的各种观念如政府、工作、权威、年龄、环境、时空和男女关系—都会影响人们的购买行为。最后，一种文化里的幽默感是很难界定的，而且这种幽默通常难以通过另一种文化领会或设释。除了具体的人口统计数据之外，很难清楚地界定或确定这些观念;而且，即使是带上文化烙印的根深蒂固的各种观念也确确实实在改变。
The target language is easily determined, but beware of generalities. The Spanish language in Spain is not the same as in Latin America. And we've all heard about the 10,000 spoken dialects in Chinese, but also realize that the “old” characters` are still used in Singapore, other nations and regions. These have largely been supplanted with “simplified” characters on China's mainland that are now, since reunification, being spread to Hong Kong SAR. Most Chinese under 40 years old on the mainland can't read the old-style writing.
目标语很容易确定，但切忌笼统概括。在西班牙使用的西班牙语与在拉丁美洲使用的西班牙语并不完全一样。我们都听说过在汉语里大约有 10,000 种口语方言，而且我们也都意识到新加坡、其他一些国家和地区还在使用繁体汉字。但在中国大陆地区，繁体字已经基本上被简化字取代了。自从香港回归以来，这一趋势也扩展到了香港特别行政区。在大陆，大多数 40 岁以下的中国人已经不会读繁体字了。
Combine superstition and language for amplified effect. In China and Japan, the number four has the same pronunciation as the word that means “death”. Consequently, a “4” in your company name or contact information might have a negative implication. The number eight, however, is considered lucky, and many products are named “88” or “888”. Phone numbers with eights denote good fortune, and real estate with eights in the address is likely to sell more quickly—especially if the price ends in “888”. These beliefs are so prevalent that hospitals in Hong Kong SAR were flooded with near-term pregnant mothers on August 8th, 1988 (8/8/88), demanding induced delivery or even Caesarian sections so their babies would have lucky birthdays. And 1988 was also the auspicious “Year of the Dragon” in the traditional Chinese calendar.
如果你能够把迷信和语言结合起来，你就能增强效果。在中国和日本，数字 4 与“死”谐音。因此，公司名字或联系信息里的数字 4 会有一种负面的含义。然而，数字 8 却被看作是一个幸运数字，于是有很多的产品名称都叫 88 或 888。有数字 8 的电话号码代表着好运。地址里含有数字 8 的房产很可能会卖得更快，特别是当价格的尾数是“888”的时候。这些数字迷信相当普遍，以致于在 1988 年 8 月 8 日(8/8/88)，香港的医院挤满了临产的孕妇，有的要求人工引产，有的甚至要求剖腹产。这样，他们的小孩就可以有幸运的生日了。. 而且，1988 年也是农历中大吉大利的龙年。
In the United States, we’re used to competitive playing field in which we constantly compare ourselves, our companies, and our products. But in the EU and much of Asia, comparisons in advertising are not accepted or allowed. Declaring that one soft-drink tastes better than another or even that one automobile is more dependable than another could be met with distaste (or even legal action). For an EU campaign, it might be okay to tout the merits of your products, but not okay to use comparative methods common to a US campaign. In some locations, citizens tend to be much more humble and self-effacing than “shoot-from-the-hip” people in the United States. Many cultures will respond better to emphasis on company longevity and reputation.
在美国，我们习惯于在竞技场上角逐，比较自身、公司和产品。但是，在欧盟和大多数亚洲国家，广告里是不接受、也不允许有比较行为的。. 如果宜称某种软饮料要比其他的软饮料口感更佳，或者某一种品牌的汽车比其他汽车更可靠，这可能会招人反感(甚至会被诉诸法律)。欧盟的宣传活动，吹捧自己产品的优点或许是可行的，但却不能采用产品比较的策略，尽管这种方法在美国是司空见惯的。. 某些地方的市民往往会比那些鲁莽行事的美国人要谦卑低调得多。在很多文化里，公司都会比较注重长期发展和公司信誉。
If you are designing visual advertising, take into account local differences in non-verbal behavior such as gestures, eye contact, personal space, and male-female relationships. Years ago, a movie was released in China that showed the first on-screen kiss ever filmed in the PRC. When the couple's lips met, an audible gasp swept through the theater. Depending on a variety of factors, this higher shock value of a public kiss could work for or against your advertising.
如果你正在策划视觉广告，那么你就有必要考虑非言语行为的地方差异，如手势、眼神交流、私人空间以及男女关系。数年前，有一部电影在中国上映，这部电影里出现了中国电影史上第一次接吻的镜头。当接吻镜头出现时，电影院里惊叹声一片。考虑到丰富的文化因素，公众之吻的较高冲击值可能会对你的广告产生截然相反的功效。
It can be a big mistake to assume a pan-Asian market or a “Latin American” or “European” buyer. Neighboring cultures elsewhere don't necessarily share buying preferences any more than a US buyer does with a Mexican consumer. Furthermore, national borders don't always delineate buying behavior; regional patterns can be just as strong.
妄加推断一个泛亚洲市场或一位拉丁美洲或欧洲客户都有可能会酿成大错。在邻国文化里，并不见得一定会有共同的购买喜好;同样，美国消费者和墨西哥消费者的购物偏好也不尽相同。而且，国界也不一定总能区分消费行为，因为地区特色也一样会很明显。
Each aspect of culture is like a stone thrown into a pool. Cuisine influences not just companies that trade in foodstuffs, but also appliances, cookware, storage ware, serve ware, packaging, as well as franchise food and hospitality companies. And don't use the Jolly Green Giant in part of Asia where a green hat worn by a man signifies that he has an unfaithful wife.
文化的方方面面都可能会如投石入水，泛起涟漪。饮食习惯不仅会影响食品公司，也会影响经营日用品、厨具、储藏器皿、餐具、包装公司，以及获得经营权的餐饮、服务店。在有些亚洲地区不要用“快乐的绿巨人”，因为在当地文化里，男人戴绿帽子就表示他妻子对他不忠。
It's definitely best to have someone with native knowledge of the target culture advise you. Small budget? Consult bi-national chambers of commerce for effective help. But before launching a marketing campaign, try a test market first, usually in a major city with demographics representative of the targeted country or region. Generally, city populations may be more sophisticated and have the most cosmopolitan attitudes; they also have the highest incomes and therefore are more able to purchase consumer and discretionary goods.
要是能够聘请到一位了解当地文化的人充当目标市场文化顾问，那肯定再好不过了。预算不够，就去咨询跨境商会以获取有效的帮助。但是，在启动一项营销活动之前，可以先到市场上测试一下，这种测试通常在目标国家或地区具有代表性的大城市进行。一般来说，城市居民见多识广，他们的观念也兼容并包;同时，他们的收人往往是最高的，更具随意购买消费品的能力。
In one such pretest, a US luggage manufacture found out that culture also affects thinking and perception. The company designed a new West Asian advertising campaign around the image of its luggage being carried on a magic flying carpet. A substantial part of the Arabic focus group thought they were seeing advertising for Samsonite carpets.
在类似这样的一次测试里，一家美国行李箱制造商发现文化同样会影响思维和感知。这家公司在中东地区策划了一则全新的广告—他们的行李箱乘坐在一块神奇的飞毯上。阿拉伯地区绝大多数的重点访谈人群则认为他们看到的是一则“Samsonite” 牌的地毯广告。

在美国，我们习惯于在竞技场上角逐，比较自身、公司和产品。但是，在欧盟和大多数亚洲国家，广告里是不接受、也不允许有比较行为的。. 如果宜称某种软饮料要比其他的软饮料口感更佳，或者某一种品牌的汽车比其他汽车更可靠，这可能会招人反感(甚至会被诉诸法律)。欧盟的宣传活动，吹捧自己产品的优点或许是可行的，但却不能采用产品比较的策略，尽管这种方法在美国是司空见惯的。. 某些地方的市民往往会比那些鲁莽行事的美国人要谦卑低调得多。在很多文化里，公司都会比较注重长期发展和公司信誉。

If you are designing visual advertising, take into account local differences in non-verbal behavior such as gestures, eye contact, personal space, and male-female relationships. Years ago, a movie was released in China that showed the first on-screen kiss ever filmed in the PRC. When the couple's lips met, an audible gasp swept through the theater. Depending on a variety of factors, this higher shock value of a public kiss could work for or against your advertising.
如果你正在策划视觉广告，那么你就有必要考虑非言语行为的地方差异，如手势、眼神交流、私人空间以及男女关系。数年前，有一部电影在中国上映，这部电影里出现了中国电影史上第一次接吻的镜头。当接吻镜头出现时，电影院里惊叹声一片。考虑到丰富的文化因素，公众之吻的较高冲击值可能会对你的广告产生截然相反的功效。

It can be a big mistake to assume a pan-Asian market or a “Latin American” or “European” buyer. Neighboring cultures elsewhere don't necessarily share buying preferences any more than a US buyer does with a Mexican consumer. Furthermore, national borders don't always delineate buying behavior; regional patterns can be just as strong.
妄加推断一个泛亚洲市场或一位拉丁美洲或欧洲客户都有可能会酿成大错。在邻国文化里，并不见得一定会有共同的购买喜好;同样，美国消费者和墨西哥消费者的购物偏好也不尽相同。而且，国界也不一定总能区分消费行为，因为地区特色也一样会很明显。

Each aspect of culture is like a stone thrown into a pool. Cuisine influences not just companies that trade in foodstuffs, but also appliances, cookware, storage ware, serve ware, packaging, as well as franchise food and hospitality companies. And don't use the Jolly Green Giant in part of Asia where a green hat worn by a man signifies that he has an unfaithful wife.
文化的方方面面都可能会如投石入水，泛起涟漪。饮食习惯不仅会影响食品公司，也会影响经营日用品、厨具、储藏器皿、餐具、包装公司，以及获得经营权的餐饮、服务店。在有些亚洲地区不要用“快乐的绿巨人”，因为在当地文化里，男人戴绿帽子就表示他妻子对他不忠。

It's definitely best to have someone with native knowledge of the target culture advise you. Small budget? Consult bi-national chambers of commerce for effective help. But before launching a marketing campaign, try a test market first, usually in a major city with demographics representative of the targeted country or region. Generally, city populations may be more sophisticated and have the most cosmopolitan attitudes; they also have the highest incomes and therefore are more able to purchase consumer and discretionary goods.
要是能够聘请到一位了解当地文化的人充当目标市场文化顾问，那肯定再好不过了。预算不够，就去咨询跨境商会以获取有效的帮助。但是，在启动一项营销活动之前，可以先到市场上测试一下，这种测试通常在目标国家或地区具有代表性的大城市进行。一般来说，城市居民见多识广，他们的观念也兼容并包;同时，他们的收人往往是最高的，更具随意购买消费品的能力。

In one such pretest, a US luggage manufacture found out that culture also affects thinking and perception. The company designed a new West Asian advertising campaign around the image of its luggage being carried on a magic flying carpet. A substantial part of the Arabic focus group thought they were seeing advertising for Samsonite carpets.
在类似这样的一次测试里，一家美国行李箱制造商发现文化同样会影响思维和感知。这家公司在中东地区策划了一则全新的广告—他们的行李箱乘坐在一块神奇的飞毯上。阿拉伯地区绝大多数的重点访谈人群则认为他们看到的是一则“Samsonite” 牌的地毯广告。

Almost all of us have heard the Nova/no va story about General Motors in Latin America, but a memorable play on words is not evidence that a marketing campaign failed. A documented example of naming adaptation is Coca-Cola in China: its Chinese name, registered in 1928, replaced local shopkeepers' attempts to represent the English sounds with Chinese characters. Sound and meaning both matter.
编者注：本文经过明确的编辑修订，纠正语言与事实错误；未经核实的包装、电影和广告轶事已改成明示的假设例子。汉字使用情况与比较广告规则也已更新。

我们几乎都听过通用汽车在拉丁美洲的 Nova/no va 故事，但一个容易记住的文字巧合，并不能证明某次营销活动失败。可口可乐在中国的命名调整则有文献记录：其于 1928 年注册的中文名称，取代了当地店主用汉字拼读英文名称的各种尝试。声音和含义都很重要。
But cultural awareness in marketing is a lot more than careful translation. There are subtleties and nuances to every culture, and there are just plain taboos. Although most people wouldn’t be able to list the rules of their own culture, they certainly know when those rules are violated. Our own culture tends to be “invisible” to us, while differences we run into when abroad strike us as strange, funny or exotic. So how much more difficult is it to discern the unwritten rules of another country?
但是市场营销中的文化意识却远远不只是小心谨慎的翻译而已。每一种文化都有它的微妙和特别之处，同时还有一些明确的禁忌。虽然大多数人都无法详尽地罗列出他们自己文化中的条条框框，但他们却肯定知道什么时候人们违背了他们的文化传统。对我们来说，自己所属的文化往往是看不见的，但是，当我们身处异地时，我们碰到的文化差异却令我们感到古怪、有趣或奇特。因此，要辨明另一国家不成文的规定又会困难多少呢？
There is still no substitute for a visit to the target market. When in a foreign place, you may become aware of different aesthetic preferences. What flavors, which colors, are used to attract buyers there? Foods you find unpalatable and decorations you find garish may appeal to local buyers. Your hosts might ask seemingly rude questions such as “How old are you?” and “How much money do you make?” Meals, schedules, transportation, and personal conveniences can't be taken for granted. Even prices for simple purchases may be open to negotiation in some settings. You haven't figured out all the small coins, and you don't understand anyone's name. And it just doesn't smell like home.
亲自走访目标市场仍然无可替代。身处异国，你可能会留意到审美偏好的差异。当地用什么口味、哪些颜色来吸引买家？你觉得难吃的食物、艳俗的装饰，或许恰好吸引当地消费者。主人可能问一些在你看来不礼貌的问题，比如“你多大了？”或“你挣多少钱？”饮食、日程安排、交通和生活便利，都不能想当然。在某些场合，即使购买普通商品，价格也可能需要商议。你还没弄懂各种小额硬币，也听不明白人们的名字。甚至气味都与家乡不同。
A visit is a golden opportunity to absorb the present-day culture. Every detail that differs from your usual pattern is a clue to the nationals. But also remember that learning the basics of comportment in another culture, though very important in your relationships with clients and contacts, isn't sufficient for planning a full marketing campaign. The simplest cultural differences can strand the grandest plans.
到目标市场走走也是吸收当今文化的黄金时机。任何与你平时生活模式有所不同的细节都能透露出当地居民的行为方式。但同样要记住的是，在培养和发展与客户或联系人的社会关系时，学会另一文化的规范行为举止虽然很重要，但这并不足以助你做一个全面的营销策划。最简单的文化差异也能搁浅最宏伟的计划。
Consider a hypothetical detergent launch in a market where small shops and limited storage space are common. A company could spend heavily on advertising and still sell very little if its large economy-size boxes did not fit store shelves or shoppers’ needs. Customers who walk to the shops might also find bulky packages difficult to carry home. This illustrates why package size, transport and storage should be researched rather than assumed from a national stereotype.
设想一个假设案例：某市场的小商店很多，储物空间有限，一家公司准备在那里推出洗衣剂。如果它的大型经济装既不适合商店货架，也不符合顾客需求，那么即使投入大量广告费用，销量仍可能很少。步行购物的顾客也可能难以把笨重的包装拎回家。这说明，包装尺寸、交通与储存条件都需要调查，不能依据对某个国家的刻板印象作出假定。
Cultural factors influence consumer behavior. These factors include religion, superstition, family structure, cuisine, language and local history but extend to attitudes about such issues as government, work, authority, age, environment, space and time, and male-female relationships. Finally, there is that difficult-to-define national sense of humor which often doesn't translate from one culture to another. Beyond concrete demographics, these attitudes are not as easy to circumscribe and pin down; besides, attitudes, even culturally ingrained ones, do change.
不同的文化因素——不仅包括宗教、迷信、家庭结构、饮食、语言和当地的历史，还延伸到对待事物的各种观念如政府、工作、权威、年龄、环境、时空和男女关系——都会影响人们的购买行为。最后，一种文化里的幽默感是很难界定的，而且这种幽默通常难以通过另一种文化领会或解释。除了具体的人口统计数据之外，很难清楚地界定或确定这些观念；而且，即使是带上文化烙印的根深蒂固的各种观念也确确实实在改变。
The target language may seem easy to identify, but beware of generalities. Spanish usage varies between Spain and Latin America and within those regions. For Chinese materials, distinguish spoken varieties from writing systems. Simplified characters are widely used in mainland China and Singapore, while traditional characters remain in use in Hong Kong SAR. Singapore aligned its simplified-character list with that of mainland China in 1976. Choose the script and vocabulary for the actual audience; do not infer an individual’s reading ability from age or nationality alone.
目标语似乎不难确定，但切忌笼统概括。西班牙与拉丁美洲的西班牙语用法有所差异，各地区内部也存在差异。制作中文材料时，要区分口语变体和书写系统。中国大陆和新加坡广泛使用简体字，香港特别行政区仍使用繁体字。新加坡在 1976 年使其简化字表与中国大陆一致。应根据实际受众选择字形和词汇，不能仅凭年龄或国籍推断个人的阅读能力。
Language and number symbolism can interact. In Mandarin, the words for four and death have similar sounds but different tones; in Japanese, shi is one reading of four and also means death. Such associations may make four unwelcome to some customers. Eight is associated with prosperity in some Chinese communities. These preferences are not universal, and a lucky number by itself does not establish that a product or property will sell faster. Test the response of the intended audience.
语言和数字象征可能相互作用。在普通话中，“四”与“死”声音相近，但声调不同；在日语中，shi 是“四”的一种读音，也是“死”的读音。这类联想可能使一些顾客不喜欢数字四。在一些华人社群中，八与兴旺富足相联系。这些偏好并非人人相同，仅凭一个吉利数字也不能断定产品或房产会卖得更快。应测试目标受众的实际反应。
Comparisons are common in U.S. advertising, but their acceptability depends on the claim, the audience and the applicable rules. The EU does not prohibit comparative advertising outright: Directive 2006/114/EC permits it when all the relevant conditions are met, including that it is not misleading and compares relevant, verifiable features objectively. Rules in Asian markets also need to be checked individually. A claim that one drink tastes better or one car is more dependable needs suitable support. Some audiences may respond better to an emphasis on company history and reputation than to aggressive comparisons.
比较在美国广告中很常见，但能否被接受，取决于具体主张、受众和适用规则。欧盟并不一概禁止比较广告：2006/114/EC 号指令允许符合全部相关条件的比较广告，其中包括不误导消费者，并客观比较相关、可验证的特征。亚洲各市场的规则也需要分别核查。声称一种饮料更好喝或一种汽车更可靠，需要适当依据。一些受众可能更看重企业的历史与信誉，而不喜欢咄咄逼人的比较。
If you are designing visual advertising, take into account local differences in non-verbal behavior such as gestures, eye contact, personal space, and male-female relationships. For a hypothetical example, imagine testing an advertisement that shows a couple kissing in public. Some viewers might find it appealing; others might be uncomfortable. The response could vary with age, setting and personal experience as well as culture, so it should be tested rather than predicted from a national label.
设计视觉广告时，应考虑非言语行为的地方差异，例如手势、眼神交流、个人空间以及男女关系。举一个假设例子：设想测试一则展示情侣当众接吻的广告，有些观众可能喜欢，有些则可能感到不自在。反应不仅可能受到文化影响，也可能因年龄、场景和个人经历而异。因此，应进行测试，而非仅凭国家标签预测。
It can be a big mistake to assume a pan-Asian market or a “Latin American” or “European” buyer. Neighboring cultures elsewhere don't necessarily share buying preferences any more than a US buyer does with a Mexican consumer. Furthermore, national borders don't always delineate buying behavior; regional patterns can be just as strong.
假定存在一个偏好一致的泛亚洲市场，或者一种统一的“拉丁美洲买家”或“欧洲买家”，可能会酿成大错。在邻国文化里，并不见得一定会有共同的购买喜好；同样，美国消费者和墨西哥消费者的购物偏好也不尽相同。而且，国界也不一定总能区分消费行为，因为地区特色也一样会很明显。
Each aspect of culture is like a stone thrown into a pool. Cuisine influences not just companies that trade in foodstuffs, but also appliances, cookware, storage ware, serve ware, packaging, as well as franchise food and hospitality companies. Even a mascot’s clothing deserves attention: the Chinese expression “wearing a green hat” mocks a man whose partner is unfaithful. That association is a reason to test a visual detail, not to assume that every green mascot will offend every Chinese viewer.
文化的各个方面都像投入池塘的石子，会激起涟漪。饮食习惯影响的不只是食品贸易公司，还包括家电、厨具、储物器皿、餐具和包装企业，以及采用特许经营模式的餐饮企业和酒店服务业。即使吉祥物的服饰也值得留意：中文里“戴绿帽子”用来讥讽伴侣有外遇的男性。这种联想说明视觉细节值得测试，并不能据此断定每个绿色吉祥物都会冒犯每一位中国观众。
It is best to seek advice from people with local knowledge of the target culture. With a small budget, bi-national chambers of commerce may be useful contacts. Before launching a campaign, try a test market whose demographics match the intended customers. A major city may be convenient, but it need not represent the whole country or region. Check income, purchasing power and demand for discretionary goods in the actual target group rather than assuming all city residents are affluent or cosmopolitan.
最好向熟悉目标文化的当地人士请教。预算有限时，可以尝试联系双边商会。启动营销活动前，应选择人口特征与目标顾客相符的市场进行测试。大城市可能较方便，却未必代表整个国家或地区。应核查实际目标群体的收入、购买力和对非必需商品的需求，不能假定所有城市居民都富裕或具有国际化观念。
As a final hypothetical example, suppose a luggage manufacturer tests an advertisement showing its suitcases on a magic flying carpet. Some participants in a focus group might think it is an advertisement for carpets rather than luggage. The example shows why testing should ask what people think the advertisement is selling, instead of assuming that an attractive image conveys the intended message.
最后再举一个假设例子：一家行李箱制造商测试一则广告，画面中它的行李箱放在神奇的飞毯上。焦点小组中的一些参与者可能以为广告卖的是地毯，而不是行李箱。这说明，测试时应该询问人们认为广告在推销什么，不能想当然地认为吸引人的画面已经传达了预期信息。

不同的文化因素——不仅包括宗教、迷信、家庭结构、饮食、语言和当地的历史，还延伸到对待事物的各种观念如政府、工作、权威、年龄、环境、时空和男女关系——都会影响人们的购买行为。最后，一种文化里的幽默感是很难界定的，而且这种幽默通常难以通过另一种文化领会或解释。除了具体的人口统计数据之外，很难清楚地界定或确定这些观念；而且，即使是带上文化烙印的根深蒂固的各种观念也确确实实在改变。

The target language may seem easy to identify, but beware of generalities. Spanish usage varies between Spain and Latin America and within those regions. For Chinese materials, distinguish spoken varieties from writing systems. Simplified characters are widely used in mainland China and Singapore, while traditional characters remain in use in Hong Kong SAR. Singapore aligned its simplified-character list with that of mainland China in 1976. Choose the script and vocabulary for the actual audience; do not infer an individual’s reading ability from age or nationality alone.
目标语似乎不难确定，但切忌笼统概括。西班牙与拉丁美洲的西班牙语用法有所差异，各地区内部也存在差异。制作中文材料时，要区分口语变体和书写系统。中国大陆和新加坡广泛使用简体字，香港特别行政区仍使用繁体字。新加坡在 1976 年使其简化字表与中国大陆一致。应根据实际受众选择字形和词汇，不能仅凭年龄或国籍推断个人的阅读能力。

Language and number symbolism can interact. In Mandarin, the words for four and death have similar sounds but different tones; in Japanese, shi is one reading of four and also means death. Such associations may make four unwelcome to some customers. Eight is associated with prosperity in some Chinese communities. These preferences are not universal, and a lucky number by itself does not establish that a product or property will sell faster. Test the response of the intended audience.
语言和数字象征可能相互作用。在普通话中，“四”与“死”声音相近，但声调不同；在日语中，shi 是“四”的一种读音，也是“死”的读音。这类联想可能使一些顾客不喜欢数字四。在一些华人社群中，八与兴旺富足相联系。这些偏好并非人人相同，仅凭一个吉利数字也不能断定产品或房产会卖得更快。应测试目标受众的实际反应。

The EU does not prohibit comparative advertising outright: Directive 2006/114/EC permits it when all the relevant conditions are met, including that it is not misleading and compares relevant, verifiable features objectively. Rules in Asian markets also need to be checked individually. A claim that one drink tastes better or one car is more dependable needs suitable support. Some audiences may respond better to an emphasis on company history and reputation than to aggressive comparisons.

If you are designing visual advertising, take into account local differences in non-verbal behavior such as gestures, eye contact, personal space, and male-female relationships. The response could vary with age, setting and personal experience as well as culture, so it should be tested rather than predicted from a national label.

It can be a big mistake to assume a pan-Asian market or a “Latin American” or “European” buyer. Neighboring cultures elsewhere don't necessarily share buying preferences any more than a US buyer does with a Mexican consumer. Furthermore, national borders don't always delineate buying behavior; regional patterns can be just as strong.

Each aspect of culture is like a stone thrown into a pool. Cuisine influences not just companies that trade in foodstuffs, but also appliances, cookware, storage ware, serve ware, packaging, as well as franchise food and hospitality companies. That association is a reason to test a visual detail, not to assume that every green mascot will offend every Chinese viewer.

corrections.before: Combine superstition and language for amplified effect. In China and Japan, the number four has the same pronunciation as the word that means “death”. Consequently, a “4” in your company name or contact information might have a negative implication. The number eight, however, is considered lucky, and many products are named “88” or “888”. Phone numbers with eights denote good fortune, and real estate with eights in the address is likely to sell more quickly—especially if the price ends in “888”. These beliefs are so prevalent that hospitals in Hong Kong SAR were flooded with near-term pregnant mothers on August 8th, 1988 (8/8/88), demanding induced delivery or even Caesarian sections so their babies would have lucky birthdays. And 1988 was also the auspicious “Year of the Dragon” in the traditional Chinese calendar.
corrections.after: Language and number symbolism can interact. In Mandarin, the words for four and death have similar sounds but different tones; in Japanese, shi is one reading of four and also means death. Such associations may make four unwelcome to some customers. Eight is associated with prosperity in some Chinese communities. These preferences are not universal, and a lucky number by itself does not establish that a product or property will sell faster. Test the response of the intended audience.

corrections.before: In the United States, we’re used to competitive playing field in which we constantly compare ourselves, our companies, and our products. But in the EU and much of Asia, comparisons in advertising are not accepted or allowed. Declaring that one soft-drink tastes better than another or even that one automobile is more dependable than another could be met with distaste (or even legal action). For an EU campaign, it might be okay to tout the merits of your products, but not okay to use comparative methods common to a US campaign. In some locations, citizens tend to be much more humble and self-effacing than “shoot-from-the-hip” people in the United States. Many cultures will respond better to emphasis on company longevity and reputation.
corrections.after: Comparisons are common in U.S. advertising, but their acceptability depends on the claim, the audience and the applicable rules. The EU does not prohibit comparative advertising outright: Directive 2006/114/EC permits it when all the relevant conditions are met, including that it is not misleading and compares relevant, verifiable features objectively. Rules in Asian markets also need to be checked individually. A claim that one drink tastes better or one car is more dependable needs suitable support. Some audiences may respond better to an emphasis on company history and reputation than to aggressive comparisons.
